misclassified_entities.reason: Internal component - SYSTEM_ADDRESS (0xff..fe) is a reserved internal address used by the protocol, not a true external entity

trusted_external_entities.name: Peer Node (Constantinople)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Remote Ethereum node propagating blocks via P2P network. Block headers and bodies require full validation including block number, timestamp, gas limit, gas used, extra data (max 32 bytes), parent hash, and difficulty.

trusted_external_entities.name: Transaction Submitter (Constantinople)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: External account or contract submitting transactions. Full validation required: intrinsic gas, ECDSA signature for sender recovery, nonce match, balance check, and 50% gas refund cap.

trusted_external_entities.name: JSON-RPC Client (Uncle Blocks)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: External application querying uncle block data via eth_getUncleByBlockHashAndIndex. Client receives baseFee field only for post-EIP-1559 blocks.

trusted_external_entities.name: Calling Contract (Block Hash History)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Smart contract requesting historical block hashes from EIP-2935 history contract. Must provide exactly 32-byte calldata with block number in valid range [current-8191, current-1].

trusted_external_entities.name: Normal Contract/EOA (History)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Regular caller interacting with history contract. Non-SYSTEM_ADDRESS callers trigger read (get) operation; write (set) operations are restricted to SYSTEM_ADDRESS.

trusted_external_entities.name: Potential Attacker (Branch Poisoning)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Malicious actor who might attempt to slow state root computation via branch poisoning. Attack cost escalates prohibitively, making it economically irrational.

trusted_external_entities.name: Transaction Submitter (London)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: User or application submitting transactions via JSON-RPC. May use legacy, EIP-2930, or EIP-1559 transaction types. Effective gas price computed from max_fee and max_priority_fee.

trusted_external_entities.name: Validator Operator (EIP-7044)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Entity holding validator signing key who can initiate voluntary exits. Signatures now use fixed Capella fork domain, making exits perpetually valid. Operator is trusted with key custody but exit signatures don't move funds.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: Full header validation required: block number, timestamp > parent, gas limit within bounds (parent +/- 1/1024), gas used <= limit, extra data <= 32 bytes, parent hash, difficulty. PoW verification via Ethash.

Constantinople transaction validation: intrinsic gas, ECDSA signature recovery, nonce match, balance check for gas + value. Gas refund capped at 50% of consumed gas. Self-destruct accounts cleaned up post-execution.
Fork state must be determined to include/omit baseFee field. Pre-EIP-1559 blocks MUST NOT include baseFee. Post-EIP-1559 blocks MUST include baseFee as Quantity type.
Calldata must be exactly 32 bytes. Block number must be in range [current-8191, current-1]. Out-of-range or malformed requests revert. Hash returned from ring buffer slot = block_number % 8191.
Non-SYSTEM_ADDRESS callers cannot write to history storage. All calls from regular addresses treated as read (get) operations. SYSTEM_ADDRESS (0xff..fe) is only authorized writer.
Economic analysis shows attack cost escalates prohibitively. Distributing funds along execution paths to degrade state root computation is not economically rational.

Transaction type detection from first byte: no prefix = legacy, 0x01 = EIP-2930, 0x02 = EIP-1559. max_fee_per_gas must be >= base_fee. Effective gas price = min(max_priority_fee, max_fee - base_fee) + base_fee.

Exit signature computed using fixed Capella fork domain, making signatures perpetually valid across future forks. Signature validation always uses CAPELLA_FORK_VERSION. Exits don't transfer funds, only initiate exit process.
